content: A standard technical standard is a formally established norm or requirement. It is typically documented in a formal manner to define uniform engineering or technical criteria, methods, processes, and practices. Additionally, a technical standard may serve as a controlled artifact or similar formal tool used for calibration purposes. Reference standards and certified reference materials are assigned values through direct comparison with a reference base. A primary standard is generally managed by a national standards body. Secondary, tertiary, check standards, and standard materials may also be utilized as references within a metrology system. A custom, convention, company product, or corporate standard that becomes widely accepted and dominant is often referred to as a de facto standard. Technical standards can be developed privately or unilaterally, such as by a corporation, regulatory body, or military organization. They can also be developed collaboratively by groups like trade unions or trade associations. Standards organizations typically involve diverse input and often create voluntary standards, which may become mandatory if adopted by a government, business contract, or similar entity. The process of standardization may occur through formal consensus among technical experts or by decree. Types of Standards 1. Standard Specification: This is a detailed set of requirements for an item, material, component, system, or service. It is often used to formalize the technical aspects of procurement agreements or contracts. For instance, a specification for a turbine blade in a jet engine would define the exact material and performance requirements. 2. Standard Test Method: This describes a definitive procedure that produces a test result. It may involve precise personal observation or highly technical measurements. For example, the physical properties of a material can depend on the specific testing method used, and any reference to such properties should include the test method employed. 3. Standard Procedure (or Standard Practice): This provides a set of instructions for performing specific operations or functions. For example, nuclear power plants have detailed standard operating procedures to ensure safe and efficient operation. 4. Standard Guide: This offers general information or options without mandating a specific course of action. 5. Standard Definition: This formally establishes terminology to ensure consistent understanding and communication. Enforcement Many standards are written as voluntary standards. Interested parties may voluntarily participate in their development, and the use of the finalized standard is also voluntary. Standards organizations typically lack the authority to enforce compliance or mandate their use. Individuals and organizations can choose whether or not to adopt a published voluntary standard. Some standards, however, are written to be mandatory. For example, a defense standard is mandatory for its intended use but may be voluntarily referenced by other organizations. Similarly, a standard published by a government regulator is mandatory for the scope of its application. When a standard is enforced by law, it is sometimes referred to as a de jure standard. Corporations may also create their own standards for mandatory internal use. In some cases, voluntary standards may become mandatory. For instance: A voluntary standard may be referenced or adopted by a government or regulatory body, making its use mandatory within the scope of its legal reference. Enforcement in such cases is carried out by the government or regulatory body that chose to reference the standard. A voluntary standard may also be adopted by a private organization or incorporated into a legal contract, making it mandatory within the context of that usage or agreement. The enforcement of a de facto standard is typically driven by free market forces. Availability Standards may be available in various forms: Public documents accessible on the internet, in public libraries, or similar venues. Some technical standards can be found in major central libraries or the libraries of reputable technical universities. Published documents available for purchase. Private documents owned by an organization or corporation, circulated as deemed necessary or useful. Documents open for public use but associated with intellectual property rights, such as copyright. Closed or controlled documents containing trade secrets or classified information. Geographic Levels When a geographically defined community needs to address a community-wide coordination problem, it can adopt an existing standard or create a new one. The primary geographic levels of standards are: National Standards: Developed by national standards organizations. Regional Standards: Created by regional standards organizations, such as CEN standards in Europe. International Standards: Established by international standards organizations, such as ISO or ASTM International. National, regional, and international standards help overcome technical barriers in inter-local or inter-regional commerce caused by differences in independently developed technical regulations and standards. Technical barriers often arise when different groups, each with a large user base, engage in mutually incompatible practices. Establishing such standards is a way to prevent or resolve these issues. Usage The existence of a published standard does not guarantee its utility or correctness. For example, compliance with a specific standard does not necessarily ensure that an item is suitable for a particular use. It is the responsibility of those who use or specify the item or service—such as engineers, trade unions, building code authorities, governments, or industries—to consider the available standards, select the appropriate one, enforce compliance, and use the item correctly. Validation of suitability is essential. Standards are often reviewed, revised, and updated. It is critical to use the most current version of a published standard. The originator or standard-writing body typically lists the latest versions on its website.
